categorias.pregunta_en: Is it raining more or less than before?
Is the land getting greener or browner?
categorias.descripcion_en: Satellite observations can help identify changes in forest condition, land cover and habitat. Ask whether a greenness change persists across years and whether it coincides with disturbance or land-use change.

categorias.pregunta_en: Are lakes and soils holding more or less water?
categorias.descripcion_en: Satellite radar can map water extent, while SWOT measures water-surface elevation. Changes can reflect seasonal inflows, evaporation and water management.

pasos.texto_en: Start with what NASA satellites measured: yearly rainfall over Nicaragua since 2001.
The slope is negative, but its 95% confidence interval includes zero: the record cannot tell a trend apart from year-to-year swings.
A second opinion: gauge-based datasets reach the same verdict.
Not significant does not mean no change. A longer record could make the same change detectable.

demostraciones.titulo_en: Tropics vs. prairies: is warming the same everywhere?

pasos.texto_en: Nicaragua's air temperature since 1981 shows a clear warming trend.
The Canadian Prairies swing by several degrees from one year to the next.
Over the same 2001–2024 window, the same method detects warming in Nicaragua but not in the noisier Prairies record.
